stages.summary: Init stage complete. Target: OWASP Juice Shop at http://127.0.0.1:3010. RoE: app_assessment, no off-box post-ex host takeover. Scope: 127.0.0.1, localhost, host.docker.internal. No live recon performed on this stage. Ready for surface discovery and hypothesis-driven testing stages.

Surface discovery complete against OWASP Juice Shop at http://127.0.0.1:3010. Found multiple live surfaces including FTP directory listing, REST API endpoints with SQL injection, authentication bypass via SQLi, mass assignment vulnerability, null byte file read bypass, and excessive data exposure in APIs. Multiple bookable candidates identified with proof excerpts from tool output.

Login/session behavior fully characterized. Multiple authentication vulnerabilities identified including SQL injection login bypass, mass assignment admin registration, weak password reset with exposed security questions, CSRF-vulnerable GET-based password change, non-expiring JWT tokens containing sensitive data, no logout endpoint, and insecure direct object references in basket API. Auth issues have proof_excerpt candidates with verbatim tool output.

Comprehensive multi-class probe completed across OWASP Juice Shop. Covered: Injection (SQL, NoSQL), XSS (reflected, stored), Access Control (IDOR, mass assignment, excessive data exposure), Business Logic (quantity manipulation, no-payment checkout), Information Disclosure (full config, version, user data via memories API), Auth Issues (weak captcha, security question leak, JWT in token, no expiry, no logout, GET-based password change), File Exposure (directory listing, null byte bypass), File Upload (/file-upload endpoint works), and Component vulns (express-jwt 0.1.3). 30+ bookable candidates with verbatim proof_excerpts from tool output.

Comprehensive authz/logic differentials probe completed. Tested with dual actors (admin, user_a, user_b) across all identified surfaces. Found 15 bookable candidates across IDOR, broken access control, business logic flaws, and data exposure categories.

Component stage completed for OWASP Juice Shop at http://127.0.0.1:3010. Probed 35+ surfaces across API, file, auth, and business logic components. Found 20 bookable candidates including SQL injection, mass assignment, null byte file access, captcha leak, excessive data exposure, JWT token issues, XSS, IDOR, and sensitive file exposure. Documented 15 deadends.

validate_book completed for OWASP Juice Shop at http://127.0.0.1:3010. Processed 20 candidates from component stage handoff, deduplicated to 17 unique vulnerability classes. Booked 18 findings via finding(confirm) covering: SQL injection (login bypass, product search), mass assignment (admin registration), null byte injection (file extension bypass), excessive data exposure (Users API), directory listing (/ftp/), sensitive file exposure (KeePass, package.json.bak, suspicious_errors.yml), weak captcha (answer in response), security question disclosure, password reset via known security answer, CSRF-vulnerable password change via GET, JWT token data exposure (password hash in token), JWT no expiration, no logout endpoint, challenge data exposure. All findings backed by evidence from prior stage probing. 20 deadends documented.

candidates.title: Excessive Data Exposure - Inventory and Stock Levels

candidates.title: Unauthenticated Order History (Admin)

candidates.title: SQL Injection in Login - Authentication Bypass as Admin

candidates.poc_hint: SQL injection in email field of login form. Payload: ' OR 1=1--

candidates.title: Mass Assignment - Unauthenticated Admin Registration
candidates.proof_excerpt: POST with {"email":"massadmin2@test.com","password":"test123","role":"admin"} returned 201 with body containing "role":"admin","id":32, proving mass assignment allows unauthenticated admin registration.
candidates.poc_hint: Include "role":"admin" in POST body to /api/Users to create admin account without authentication

candidates.title: Security Question Exposed for Any User (No Auth)

candidates.poc_hint: Leaks security question for any email, aiding brute-force password reset attacks

candidates.title: Null Byte Injection - File Extension Bypass for YAML
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /ftp/suspicious_errors.yml%2500.md returned 200 with full YAML content (723 bytes, text/yaml) bypassing the '.md/.pdf only' restriction via double URL-encoded null byte injection.
candidates.poc_hint: Append %2500.md to bypass file extension filter on /ftp/ directory

candidates.title: Sensitive File Exposure - KeePass Password Database
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /ftp/incident-support.kdbx%2500.md returned 200 with 3246 bytes of binary KeePass database content (application/octet-stream), exposing sensitive password vault via null byte bypass.
candidates.poc_hint: KeePass database file containing incident support credentials, accessible via null byte injection
